content: 1. Tetracycline can increase the plasma concentration or pharmacological effect of rimegepant by altering the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. This necessitates careful monitoring or adjustment of therapy. 2. Metronidazole can elevate the levels or effects of rimegepant by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is advised. Additionally, rimegepant should not be redosed within 48 hours if co-administered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. 3. Metronidazole can increase the levels or effects of ritonavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 4. Rucaparib can elevate the levels or effects of tetracycline by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. Dosage adjustments of CYP3A4 substrates may be necessary if clinically indicated. 5. Tetracycline can increase the levels or effects of ruxolitinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, metronidazole can also elevate ruxolitinib levels or effects via the same mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 6. Tetracycline and metronidazole can increase the levels or effects of topical ruxolitinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 7. Bismuth subsalicylate can reduce the levels or effects of sarecycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. 8. Products containing multivalent cations may impair the absorption of tetracyclines, potentially reducing their efficacy. It is advised to separate the dosing of tetracyclines from these products. 9. Metronidazole can increase the levels of seladelpar by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Patients who are poor CYP2C9 metabolizers and are taking seladelpar with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should be monitored closely. 10. Tetracycline can decrease the effects of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering metabolism. Similarly, metronidazole can reduce the effects of this combination. Caution and monitoring are advised. To avoid magnesium chelation, tetracycline should be taken at least 2 hours before and no less than 6 hours after the administration of sodium picosulfate, magnesium oxide, and anhydrous citric acid. 11. Metronidazole can increase the levels or effects of solifenacin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 12. Tetracycline can elevate the levels or effects of sonidegib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. Co-administration of sonidegib with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided. If a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used, it should be administered for less than 14 days, with close monitoring for adverse reactions, particularly musculoskeletal effects. 13. Metronidazole can increase the levels or effects of sonidegib via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. Avoid co-administration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors unless necessary, and limit their use to less than 14 days with close monitoring. 14. Bismuth subsalicylate and sotalol may interact through pharmacodynamic synergism, potentially causing severe hypertension due to renal prostaglandin synthesis blockade. Caution and monitoring are advised. 15. Tetracycline can increase the levels or effects of sparsentan by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required, but no dosage adjustment is necessary. Blood pressure, serum potassium, edema, and kidney function should be monitored regularly when sparsentan is co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 16. Stiripentol, a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer, can affect the metabolism of tetracycline. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. CYP3A4 substrates co-administered with stiripentol may require dosage adjustments. 17. Metronidazole can increase the levels or effects of sufentanil SL by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase sufentanil plasma concentrations, potentially leading to prolonged or severe adverse effects, including fatal respiratory depression. 18. Tetracycline can also increase the levels or effects of sufentanil SL via CYP3A4 metabolism. Similar precautions apply as with metronidazole. 19. Metronidazole and sulfamethoxazole may interact by decreasing metabolism, potentially causing a disulfiram-like reaction. Caution and monitoring are advised. 20. Metronidazole can increase the levels or effects of sunitinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 21. Tetracycline can elevate the levels or effects of suvorexant by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. The starting dose of suvorexant should be reduced to 5 mg at bedtime if co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 22. Metronidazole can also increase the levels or effects of suvorexant via CYP3A4 metabolism. Similar precautions apply as with tetracycline. 23. Metronidazole can increase the levels or effects of tacrolimus by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 24. Tetracycline can elevate the levels or effects of tadalafil by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary, as CYP3A4 inhibitors may reduce tadalafil clearance, increasing systemic exposure and the risk of adverse events. 25. Metronidazole can also increase the levels or effects of tadalafil via CYP3A4 metabolism. Similar precautions apply as with tetracycline. 26. Metronidazole can increase the levels or effects of tamoxifen by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required, as CYP3A4 inhibition decreases the metabolism of tamoxifen to its active metabolite, N-desmethyl tamoxifen. 27. Metronidazole can elevate the levels of tamsulosin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction may be necessary for drugs predominantly metabolized by CYP3A4. 28. Tazemetostat can decrease the levels or effects of tetracycline by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 29. Tecovirimat, a weak CYP3A4 inducer, can reduce the levels or effects of tetracycline by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates is recommended. 30. Metronidazole can increase the levels or effects of temsirolimus by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 31. Metronidazole can elevate the levels or effects of tezacaftor by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. Dosage adjustments of tezacaftor may be required when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 32. Tetracycline can also increase the levels or effects of tezacaftor via CYP3A4 metabolism. Similar precautions apply as with metronidazole. 33. Metronidazole can increase the levels or effects of theophylline by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 34. Bismuth subsalicylate and timolol may interact through pharmacodynamic synergism, potentially causing severe hypertension due to renal prostaglandin synthesis blockade. Caution and monitoring are advised. 35. Tetracycline can increase the levels or effects of tinidazole by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. 36. Metronidazole can also elevate the levels or effects of tinidazole via CYP3A4 metabolism. Similar precautions apply as with tetracycline. 37. Metronidazole can increase the levels or effects of tipranavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 38. Tobramycin inhaled and bismuth subsalicylate can both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Concurrent or sequential use should be avoided to reduce the risk of ototoxicity. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 39. Tetracycline can increase the levels of tofacitinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. No specific dose adjustment is recommended when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, but the dose should be reduced if co-administered with both moderate CYP3A4 and potent CYP2C19 inhibitors. 40. Metronidazole can also elevate the levels of tofacitinib via CYP3A4 metabolism. Similar precautions apply as with tetracycline. 41. Metronidazole can increase the levels or effects of acetaminophen (oral, IV, or rectal) by affecting CYP2E1 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 42. Acetazolamide can increase the levels or effects of tetracycline by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 43. Metronidazole can elevate the levels or effects of alfentanil by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 44. Metronidazole can increase the levels or effects of alfuzosin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 45. Metronidazole can elevate the levels or effects of alosetron by affecting CYP2C9/10 or CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 46. Metronidazole can increase the levels or effects of amitriptyline by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 47. Anastrozole can elevate the levels or effects of tetracycline by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 48. Tetracycline can enhance the effects of antithrombin alfa, antithrombin III, or argatroban through pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. 49. Metronidazole can increase the levels or effects of armodafinil by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 50. Bismuth subsalicylate can enhance the effects of aspirin (oral, rectal, or in combination with citric acid and sodium bicarbonate) through pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. 51. Metronidazole can increase the levels or effects of atazanavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 52. Tetracycline can reduce the levels of atovaquone by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 53. Metronidazole can decrease the levels or effects of balsalazide by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. 54. Tetracycline can also reduce the levels or effects of balsalazide by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 55. Tetracycline can enhance the effects of bemiparin through pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 56. Metronidazole can reduce the levels or effects of biotin by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 57. Tetracycline can also reduce the levels or effects of biotin by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 58. Tetracycline can enhance the effects of bivalirudin through pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 59. Metronidazole can increase the levels or effects of bosentan by affecting CYP2C9/10 or CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 60. Metronidazole can elevate the levels or effects of celecoxib by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 61. Metronidazole can increase the levels or effects of cevimeline by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 62. Metronidazole can elevate the levels or effects of clarithromycin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 63. Metronidazole can increase the levels or effects of clomipramine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 64. Colestipol can reduce the levels of tetracycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 65. Cyclophosphamide can elevate the levels or effects of tetracycline by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 66. Tetracycline can enhance the effects of dalteparin through pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 67. Danazol can increase the levels or effects of tetracycline by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 68. Metronidazole can elevate the levels or effects of dapsone by affecting CYP2E1 or CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 69. Metronidazole can increase the levels or effects of diclofenac by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown.
